title: Print-optimized invoice document layout and print/PDF workflow

requirements.summary: Add a dedicated print-optimized invoice document layout (separate from the on-screen invoice detail UI) that includes core invoice info and excludes navigation/actions/photos/edit/payment UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking Print from the invoice detail page prints a document-style invoice layout (not cards/buttons/tabs from the app UI).
The printed output does not include the top action bar (Back/Print/Download/Edit) and does not include Before/After photo sections.

The printed output includes: business logo, invoice number, paid/unpaid status, customer name and contact info (when available), BUSINESS_ADDRESS (and TEXT_NUMBER when non-empty), line item table, total amount due, amount paid, balance, and PAYMENT_INSTRUCTIONS.
The printed output is legible in black-and-white printing and does not depend on the app’s on-screen grid/card layout to look correct.

file_operations.description: Create a reusable, print-first invoice document component that renders only invoice document content (logo using INVOICE_LOGO, invoice number, paid/unpaid status, customer details when available, BUSINESS_ADDRESS and optional TEXT_NUMBER, line-items table, totals with amount due/paid/balance, and PAYMENT_INSTRUCTIONS). Ensure it does not render any app navigation, action buttons, photo sections, or edit/payment UI. Keep styling document-oriented and black-and-white friendly (avoid reliance on card/grid UI).

Remove/disable the current print-only header block that attempts to print the on-screen layout, and ensure the invoice detail page remains a screen-optimized view (photos, payments, edit) while the dedicated InvoiceDocument layout is used only for printing/downloading.

requirements.summary: Update Print and Download PDF actions to use the dedicated invoice document layout via a print-only view/route that auto-triggers browser print.
acceptanceCriteria: Print uses the dedicated invoice document layout.
Download PDF uses the same dedicated invoice document layout and results in a browser print dialog suitable for saving as PDF.
No additional backend calls are required beyond the existing invoice/customer queries already used for the invoice detail page.

file_operations.description: Create a print-only invoice view that loads invoice/customer data using the existing invoice/customer query hooks and renders InvoiceDocument only. After the document is ready, trigger the browser print dialog (and optionally close the window after printing when opened in a new tab). Do not introduce any additional data fetching beyond what the invoice detail page already uses.
Register a new route for the print-only invoice view (e.g., a nested route under invoices with the invoiceId param) so it can be navigated to directly and renders the InvoicePrintPage.

Change the Print and Download PDF actions to open/navigate to the print-only invoice route so printing/downloading uses the dedicated InvoiceDocument layout rather than window.print() on the current screen UI. Keep the on-screen invoice detail page layout otherwise unchanged.

requirements.summary: Extend print CSS to ensure consistent page size/margins and improved page-break behavior for invoice documents, without changing the on-screen invoice detail UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Printed invoice uses consistent page margins and a standard page size already used by the app’s print rules (e.g., letter).
Line items table does not break mid-row; major sections avoid splitting across pages when feasible.
Non-print (screen) layout remains functional and visually unchanged aside from Print/Download behavior improvements.

file_operations.description: Update/extend @media print rules to better support a document-style invoice: keep letter sizing and margins, add page-break control for invoice sections and the line-items table (avoid breaking mid-row), and ensure print-specific typography/spacing is consistent. Ensure changes are scoped to print/document classes so the normal screen UI remains unchanged.

Add print-hiding behavior for global app chrome (header/nav/footer) by applying the existing no-print class to BrandHeader, the nav bar, and the footer so they never appear in printed output, especially when printing from the dedicated print route.
